blocks.text: Quick verdict

ProxyEmpire is the better choice for rotating residential and mobile work such as scraping and ad verification: it publishes its pool, includes city and ISP targeting, supports 24-hour sticky sessions and never expires prepaid traffic. Proxys.io is the better choice when you need fixed IPs for long-lived accounts, cheap bulk IPv6, or flat-rate mobile proxies with unlimited bandwidth, and its 24-hour refund window protects you if the IPs do not suit your platform.

Proxys.io and ProxyEmpire both sell residential, mobile and static proxies, but their core products differ. Proxys.io is a provider of rotating residential traffic and monthly rentals: you can rent individual IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, premium residential IPs or mobile proxies for a set period, with unlimited traffic specifically confirmed for dedicated mobile IPv4 on a private channel. ProxyEmpire is a rotating pool provider with 30M+ advertised residential IPs, free ISP targeting and bandwidth that never expires. This comparison helps you decide which model suits your workload.

blocks.text: Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

PROXYS.IO offers both rented static addresses and a rotating residential network. The provider reports more than 100 million ISP addresses across 195 countries, country/region/city targeting, up to 100 saved parameter sets and rotation every 2-60 minutes. Its mobile service covers 14 countries with city/carrier selection and roughly 2,000-5,000 addresses per country/carrier combination. Static IPv4 covers 24 markets. These are supplied specifications, not independently measured availability. HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 are included on every plan.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
ProxyEmpire in 2026: what you get

ProxyEmpire is a Bulgarian-registered provider (SWIFT SAAS LTD) that has been selling since 2020. Its residential and mobile networks share one system with 30M+ advertised IPs in 170+ countries, and country, region, city and ISP targeting are included at no extra cost. The standout policy is bandwidth rollover: prepaid traffic carries forward indefinitely, even after a subscription lapses. Proxyway's 2026 market tests found ProxyEmpire's pool was the third largest among the providers it tested.

Strengths: Prepaid traffic rolls over indefinitely; ISP/ASN targeting included at no extra cost; Cheap $1.97 trial covering residential and mobile; Unlimited residential option priced per day. Weak spots: Smaller advertised pool than the big three; Exact GB thresholds for each tier only shown at checkout; Weaker results on Google in some independent tests.
Pricing: Proxys.io vs ProxyEmpire

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

ProxyEmpire's rotating residential pricing currently starts at $3.50/GB (shown as 50% off a $7 list price) and steps down through several tiers to $1.50/GB at 1 TB, with custom pricing from about $0.75/GB above 5 TB. Rotating mobile starts at $4.50/GB, rotating datacenter at about $0.65/GB, and a flat-rate unlimited residential plan is sold by the day.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; ProxyEmpire comes to about $35. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io and ProxyEmpire do not publish an exact price for that volume. Look past the per-GB figure too. ProxyEmpire lets unused traffic carry forward, while Proxys.io's allowance does not (30/60/90-day traffic validity; minimum one-month static rental). For irregular workloads, that difference can outweigh a small gap in list price.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

PROXYS.IO reports a residential pool of 100M+ ISP addresses; this has not been independently audited. Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses and ProxyEmpire lists '30M+'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage countries and ProxyEmpire lists 170+. On targeting, Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile, while ProxyEmpire offers country, region, city and ISP/ASN (included by default).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile, and ProxyEmpire offers rotating or sticky sessions up to 24 hours. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: compare the exact target and traffic plan before choosing. PROXYS.IO reports a 100M+ rotating residential network across 195 countries, in addition to static rentals. Pool size alone does not establish success rate; this brief does not independently benchmark PROXYS.IO against the other provider.

SERP and rank tracking: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Proxys.io: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks. With ProxyEmpire: Google was its weakest target in independent tests. Run the same small test on both before committing.

Social media and multi-account management: Proxys.io. Proxys.io has the edge here. Why: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. How ProxyEmpire compares: residential and mobile IPs with 24-hour sticky sessions.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: ProxyEmpire. ProxyEmpire has the edge here. Why: free city and ISP targeting. How Proxys.io compares: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.
Ad verification and geo-testing: ProxyEmpire. ProxyEmpire has the edge here. Why: ISP-level targeting at no extra cost. How Proxys.io compares: limited geo depth.

Tight budgets: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Proxys.io: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth. ProxyEmpire: rollover means nothing you pay for is wasted. Let price and the countries you need decide.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile. Verification and payment rules differ too. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. ProxyEmpire: Standard verification. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Proxys.io and ProxyEmpire before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle Proxys.io vs ProxyEmpire faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial; ProxyEmpire: $1.97 trial with 100 MB residential and 50 MB mobile).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Proxys.io comes out ahead in 1, ProxyEmpire in 3, and 2 are ties. That makes ProxyEmpire the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs, while ProxyEmpire is strongest for teams that hate losing unused bandwidth. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
